newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bank stocks rise after rates left unchanged.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bank stocks rise after rates left unchanged.

text.p: U.S. bank stocks rose Tuesday after the Federal Reserve left short term interest rates unchanged.
The news from the Fed ended a period of speculation about whether the Fed would raise rates again after having increased the key federal funds rate to 5.50 percent on March 25.

"Large capitalization bank stocks and most other bank stocks have been selling off on interest rate fears," said Raphael Soifer, analyst at Brown Brothers Harriman. "What we see now is the stocks taking some of that ground back."
Chase Manhattan Corp was up 2-1/2 to 95-1/8, Citicorp was up 2-1/4 to 118-1/4 and First Union Corp was up 1-3/8 to 85-5/8.
Soifer, who tracks money center banks including Chase and Citicorp, said he expects those two stocks to get back to their old highs by the end of the year.
Chase hit a high of 110-1/2 earlier this year and Citicorp hit a high of 127-1/8.
Soifer and other analysts have argued that bank earnings are not impacted much by interest rate changes. But the analysts have noted the stocks react strongly to rate changes.
